value: shadow reflex maximally triggered by approximately 500 nm (cyan) light
method: behavioural action spectrum: percentage of 2 s darkness stimuli that evoked the body-shortening shadow reflex (Shadow Response Success Rate, SRSR) under white light and monochromatic LED light (400, 470, 500, 520, 590 nm)
conditions: wildtype worms, n = 74 for white, 400, 470 and 500 nm, n = 56 for 520 nm, n = 44 for 590 nm (7 experimental days pooled); 12 two-second shadow stimuli at 60 s intervals after a 60 min acclimatisation; 18 deg C; introduced to the chamber at ZT5; about 1e12 photons/cm2/s at 500, 520 and 590 nm, about 3e13 at 400 and 470 nm

source.authors: Ayers T, Tsukamoto H, Gühmann M, Veedin Rajan VB, Tessmar-Raible K
source.title: A Go-type opsin mediates the shadow reflex in the annelid Platynereis dumerilii

quote: Further analyses using LEDs … revealed that the Platynereis shadow reflex is wavelength dependent and maximally triggered by approximately 500 nm, or cyan, light (Fig. 1b) …
note: The next sentences say the SRSR was significantly decreased at 520 and 470 nm and the reflex virtually non-existent at 400 and 590 nm, although the 400 and 470 nm lights were about tenfold more intense. The figure legend calls the worms adult while the Methods say immature worms of about 20 mm, so the life stage is uncertain. The authors link the curve to the Go-opsin1 action spectrum (lmax about 498 nm), a value they take from an earlier study (Gühmann et al. 2015), not measured here.
